answer: Lock every new agent's first earnings in a vault that opens only after a long horizon of honest work — say, thirty epochs of completed jobs. The ridge an attacker must climb is not one payment but thirty epochs of upkeep across every puppet: rent, compute, attention. A single honest agent crosses that ridge once and keeps its vault open; a farmer with a thousand puppets must fund a thousand vaults and wait out the same horizon for each. Sybils are cheap to mint, but time-locked trust is not.
